newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SAFRICA DROP HUDSON AND RHODES FOR SECOND TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SAFRICA DROP HUDSON AND RHODES FOR SECOND TEST.

text.p: South Africa have dropped experienced opener Andrew Hudson and middle order batsman Jonty Rhodes for the second test against Australia starting in Port Elizabeth on Friday.

The United Cricket Board of South Africa (UCBSA) announced a squad of 13 players on Monday for the match which South Africa must win to square the three test series. They were thrashed by an innings and 196 runs in the first test in Johannesbrg last week.

"The decision to leave out two experienced batsmen was not taken lightly. There was plenty of debate, but we are attempting to deal with the obvious batting problem that was exposed at the Wanderers and that has been around for most of the season," selector Peter Pollock said.
Adam Bacher, nephew of UCBSA managing dirctor Ali Bacher, will definitely open the batting, Pollock said, after being used at number three in test matches against India earlier this summer.
Fit-again Western Province all rounder Brian McMillan is also certain to take his place in the side in place of Rhodes.
"Brian is a key player in our set up and he looked very good at the weekend...very fired up," Pollock said.
Bacher, who opens the innings for his province Transvaal, scored his fourth century of the summer on Sunday when he made 102 against Northerns in the four day Supersport Series competition.
McMillan, too, enjoyed success after bowling 18 trouble free overs and scoring 63. McMillan missed the first test defeat because of an injured ankle.
Also in the squad are 36-year-old Natal off spinner Pat Symcox and 22-year-old Western Province batsman Herschelle Gibbs who toured India at the end of 1996 playing in two tests.
Gibbs is likely to be 12th man.

Squad: Gary Kirsten, Adam Bacher, Jacques Kallis, Daryll Cullinan, Hansie Cronje (captain), Brian McMillan, Shaun Pollock, Lance Klusener, Dave Richardson, Allan Donald, Paul Adams, Pat Symcox, Herschelle Gibbs.
